headline: A quiet, mild Thursday gives way to a chilly weekend: a Friday front brings spotty Kentucky showers, then frost and freeze risk expands
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Drier air behind Wednesday’s front is eroding early low cloud and valley fog, allowing a seasonable and mainly sunny Thursday. A compact cold-core disturbance and reinforcing northwest front arrive Friday. Shallow low-level moisture beneath cold air aloft favors clouds, patchy drizzle or a few light showers, followed by steady cold advection. High pressure then builds in Saturday, supporting a dry but chilly day and strong radiational cooling Saturday night. The resulting frost and freeze risk is the period’s principal hazard.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 6:55 AM EST, KDVK reported 50°F with a 48°F dew point, southwest wind near 3 mph, visibility above 10 miles and clear sky after earlier mist. At 6:54 AM, KLEX reported 52°F with a 52°F dew point, southwest wind near 6 mph, 6-mile visibility in mist and clear sky. The main rain shield was east of Central Kentucky. An official NWS Special Weather Statement for patchy fog includes Boyle County through 9:00 AM EST, although conditions at KDVK had already improved.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS SPECIAL WEATHER STATEMENT: Boyle County is included through 9:00 AM EST for patchy fog reducing visibility below one mile at times, mainly in low-lying rural areas. No other official point alert is active. Separate independent concern is patchy late-night valley fog after recent heavy rain; locally sub-mile visibility is possible, but widespread dense fog is not the primary outcome.
days.forecast: Morning low cloud and isolated valley fog erode after sunrise as southwest mixing increases. Sunshine then dominates, with a most-likely Danville high near 66°F. Southwest wind runs 4–10 mph with afternoon gusts around 15–20 mph. Clouds begin increasing from the north late tonight ahead of the next disturbance. Fresh BUFKIT profiles show a meaningful near-saturation signal overnight, so patchy valley fog remains possible before the thicker cloud shield arrives. Applying the established KDVK low correction, the most-likely Danville low is near 43°F.

days.label: Friday
days.precipitation: 25–35%, mainly afternoon and evening; trace to 0.05 inch
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active for Friday at issuance. The official Louisville discussion highlights Friday-night frost and a sharper weekend freeze. Independent concerns are spotty drizzle or light showers, a breezy temperature fall, and frost with isolated near-freezing rural readings late Friday night.
days.forecast: Clouds thicken as a cold-core shortwave and reinforcing front cross the region. Saturation is shallow and cloud ice is limited, favoring patchy drizzle or light showers rather than meaningful rain; the best chance is afternoon into evening and amounts should be only a trace to 0.05 inch. The high most likely reaches 58°F before temperatures fall through the 50s behind the boundary. West wind turns northwest at 5–12 mph with gusts around 15–25 mph. Clouds begin breaking Friday night, allowing patchy frost. After the KDVK correction, the most-likely Danville low is near 33°F, with colder rural pockets near 30°F.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert is active for Saturday at issuance. OFFICIAL NWS DISCUSSION: the Bluegrass has a 60–90% NBM probability of falling below 32°F Saturday night and a 30–50% probability of 28°F or colder in favored rural low spots. Independent concern is widespread frost and a likely freeze by Sunday morning.
days.forecast: Cold advection continues despite partly to mostly sunny skies. The most-likely Danville high is near 53°F, with north to northwest wind around 5–10 mph and gusts of 15–20 mph. High pressure settles overhead Saturday night, reducing wind and maximizing radiational cooling. Widespread frost is likely; the most-likely Danville low is near 29°F after the established correction, while rural Bluegrass hollows may reach the middle 20s. Sensitive outdoor vegetation and livestock forage exposed to a hard freeze may need protection.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky is dry and seasonable today, with a most-likely Danville high near 66°F. A reinforcing front Friday brings clouds, a 25–35% chance of patchy drizzle or light showers, and temperatures falling through the 50s. Saturday is dry and chilly near 53°F. The main concern is the weekend cold: patchy frost is possible late Friday night, followed by widespread frost and a likely freeze Saturday night into Sunday morning. Most-likely bias-corrected Danville lows are 43°F, 33°F and 29°F.
kentucky.confidence: High on today’s dry weather and clearing; moderate-high on today’s high; moderate on Friday shower coverage and exact afternoon high; high on Saturday dryness; moderate-high on widespread Saturday-night frost/freeze but lower on the coldest rural minimum

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: The organized overnight rain band has shifted east, but a humid boundary layer remains trapped beneath widespread low stratus. Patchy fog and residual showers continue this morning. Weak instability can support an isolated rumble of thunder, yet forcing and stronger shear overlap poorly, keeping severe weather unlikely. A diffuse front crosses Friday and brings drier air, while high pressure strengthens Saturday. The largest forecast question is Saturday’s temperature: a short-range RRFS cold cluster keeps highs near 60°F, but the official forecast, GFS, GEFS, ECMWF and NBM consensus favors upper 60s under sunshine.
upstate.currentConditions: At 6:54 AM EST, KCEU was 68°F with a 68°F dew point, calm wind, 6-mile visibility in mist and overcast cloud near 200 feet. At 6:55 AM, KLQK was 68°F with a 66°F dew point, south-southwest wind near 7 mph, 7-mile visibility and overcast cloud near 200 feet. No official NWS point alert was active for Clemson or Central. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Thursday
days.precipitation: 30–50% through early afternoon; 15–30% late afternoon and evening; 20–30% overnight
days.hazard: OFFICIAL OUTLOOKS: SPC forecasts no severe-thunderstorm area today, and WPC says no excessive-rainfall area is expected. No active NWS point alert is in effect. Independent concerns are morning fog, low visibility and a few residual showers; an isolated rumble of thunder is possible, but severe weather and flooding are unlikely.
days.forecast: IFR stratus and mist linger this morning as the main overnight rain band pulls east. Spotty showers remain possible through early afternoon, followed by a lull; another small shower chance returns tonight as the front nears, but generally 0.10 inch or less of additional rain is expected, with an isolated total near 0.15 inch. Weak instability may produce a brief rumble of thunder, but poor overlap with stronger shear sharply limits severe potential. Partial breaks can lift the most-likely high to 75°F. Southwest wind runs 2–7 mph with gusts around 10–18 mph. IFR stratus and patchy fog may redevelop tonight. After the station corrections, the most-likely lows are near 61°F at Clemson and 56°F around Central/Pickens.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL SPC DAY 2: A Marginal Risk is confined to the eastern Carolinas and far southeast Virginia; Clemson and Central are outside it. No active NWS point alert is in effect. Independent concern is patchy morning fog and locally sub-mile visibility before rapid improvement; no threshold severe or flooding hazard is expected.
days.forecast: Patchy fog and low stratus may briefly be dense around sunrise, then the front crosses and drier northwest flow produces rapid improvement to mostly sunny conditions. The most-likely high is near 75°F; the short-range guidance is a little cooler, but the official forecast and broader multi-model center favor the middle 70s. North to northwest wind runs 1–6 mph with gusts around 8–15 mph. A clear, cooler night follows. Applying the station corrections, the most-likely lows are near 50°F at Clemson and 45°F around Central/Pickens.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: OFFICIAL SPC DAY 3: No thunderstorm area is forecast. No active NWS point alert is in effect. No threshold independent hazard is expected in the Clemson–Central corridor; patchy frost is possible only in the coldest sheltered rural pockets late Saturday night.
days.forecast: High pressure brings a sunny and cooler day. The established 72-hour verified blend of GFS, ECMWF and GEFS centers near 69°F, in close agreement with the official forecast and NBM, so the most-likely high is 68–69°F. A correlated RRFS/BUFKIT cold cluster near 59–63°F is retained as a lower-probability outcome only if stronger cold advection or unexpected morning stratocumulus persists. North wind around 2–6 mph becomes light late. Applying the station corrections, the most-likely overnight lows are near 45°F at Clemson and 40°F around Central/Pickens; colder sheltered pockets may reach the upper 30s.

upstate.bottomLine: Morning fog, low cloud and a 30–50% residual shower chance give way to gradual improvement today; severe weather and excessive rain are not expected. Friday begins with patchy fog, then turns dry and mostly sunny near 75°F. Saturday is sunny and cooler, most likely 68–69°F. The short-range 59–63°F Saturday branch is lower probability because the official forecast, global models, GEFS and NBM favor the upper 60s. Bias-corrected most-likely lows are Clemson 61°F, 50°F and 45°F; Central/Pickens 56°F, 45°F and 40°F.
upstate.confidence: Moderate-high on today’s fog and gradual improvement; moderate on residual shower placement; high on Friday drying; moderate-high on Friday high; moderate on Saturday high because of the resolved cold-cluster alternative; high on the dry weekend

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERT: the NWS Louisville Special Weather Statement issued at 6:53 AM EST includes Boyle County through 9:00 AM for patchy fog that can reduce visibility below one mile in low-lying rural areas. No active point alert was found for Clemson or Central at the final checks. Official alerts remain explicitly separate from official outlooks and this independent analysis.

The newest 11:31Z Louisville discussion expects early low cloud and fog to erode, afternoon temperatures in the lower to middle 60s, patchy Friday drizzle or light showers, Friday-night frost and a more widespread Saturday-night freeze. No LMK watch, warning or advisory was active.

The newest 11:33Z Greenville-Spartanburg discussion says the heaviest rain has exited, a lull follows with only 15–35% afternoon/evening rain chances, another IFR/LIFR stratus bout is possible tonight, and a Friday cold front begins a dry weekend. The 10:49Z zone forecast supports middle-70s highs today and Friday and upper 60s Saturday.

Official outlooks are distinct from point alerts: SPC has no severe area today; Friday's Marginal Risk is confined to the eastern Carolinas and far southeast Virginia, outside Clemson and Central; SPC forecasts no thunder area Saturday. WPC says no Day 1 excessive-rainfall area is expected.

Latest official observations show the post-frontal cloud deck already breaking around Lexington and Danville; KDVK improved from earlier mist to clear sky and visibility above 10 miles by 6:55 AM, while KCEU and KLQK remain in 200-foot overcast with mist reported at KCEU. Tempest was excluded.

College of DuPage 11:21–11:31Z imagery shows the organized rain shield east of Central Kentucky, clearing or thinning cloud over Kentucky, the Upstate's overnight band shifting east, and a lingering broad low-cloud shield across the western Carolinas.

Chris Bailey’s exact November 5 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘A Chilly November Weekend Ahead,’ and its supporting graphics were consulted as accepted source material. Bailey calls for 60s and partial sun today, a Friday front with clouds, wind, scattered afternoon/evening showers and falling 50s, Saturday highs mainly 50–55, and upper-20s readings for many by Sunday morning. Details absent from the post or unreadable in its graphics were left unknown.

Central Kentucky guidance is coherent today near the middle 60s. Friday guidance spans roughly 52–60°F as shallow cloud and drizzle timing varies; the candidate resolves this with a 58°F most-likely value and calibrated 55–60°F range. Saturday's weighted center is near 52–54°F, consistent with Bailey and the official forecast.

The official Louisville discussion gives the Bluegrass a 60–90% NBM probability of falling below 32°F Saturday night and a 30–50% probability of 28°F or colder in favored rural low spots. The independent 29°F Danville center incorporates the established −2°F KDVK low correction.

Fresh BUFKIT profiles support a meaningful Danville-area saturation and fog signal tonight, so patchy fog is retained despite its absence from the point forecast. The Friday cloud layer is shallow and often lacks ice, favoring drizzle or light showers with little accumulation.

Upstate remaining rainfall was normalized to the post-issuance period. Official guidance gives less than 0.10 inch, while the deterministic and ensemble core generally supports 0.10 inch or less and only an isolated amount near 0.15 inch. No heavy-rain hazard is carried forward.

For Saturday in the Upstate, RRFS/BUFKIT forms a correlated 59–63°F cold cluster. The official forecast near 69°F, GFS near 70°F, GEFS median 69.6°F, ECMWF near 66°F and NBM in the upper 60s support the warmer branch. The established complete-family blend centers near 69°F; the cold cluster remains a disclosed lower-probability conditional outcome rather than an unresolved blocker.
